blocks.text: Alerts are triggered to notify you about anomalous activities related to identities. Alerts provide details about the detected activity, associated user or entity, and the risk level. Alerts for similar kinds of anomalous activities are correlated and grouped into incidents to help security teams investigate potential threats and remediate issues. Alerts aggregate data from different sources such as ITDR Change Detection AD and ITDR Change Detection Entra.
Alerts provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Review alerts aggregated from different sources to get in-depth insights about identity-related threats across your organization.
Review the alert details and remediate the issues.

blocks.text: On the Alerts page (Identities > Alerts), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Select from system-saved views or views you previously saved.
Search for an alert.
Save the current view.
Filter the alert information.
View the number of alerts triggered for each integrated product (e.g., Okta, Gmail).
View the distribution of alerts across different severity score ranges, and identify the overall risk level to prioritize high severity alerts and remediate the issues.

View the number of alerts detected, the number of incidents created by grouping similar types of alerts, and the number of active incidents. This overview depicts the alert volume versus the actual investigated incidents.
Select alerts from the list, and click Update to change the settings.
See instructions.
Severity: Select the severity level for the alert (Critical, High, Low, Medium, or None).
Status: Select the status for the alert (Discovered, Acknowledged, Remediated or Confirmed).
Title: Enter a title for the alert.
Verdict: Select the inference for the alert (Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious, or True Positive).
Click Save.
See image.
Select similar alerts from the list, and click Create Incident to create a new incident from the selected alerts.
See instructions.
In the Create Incident from Alerts window:
Severity: Select the severity level for an incident (Critical, High, Low, Medium, or None).
Status: Select the status for an incident (New, Acknowledged, Remediated, Pending Remediation, or Closed).
Title: Enter a title for the incident.
Verdict: Select the inference for the incident (Benign, False Positive, Inconclusive, Malicious, Suspicious, or True Positive).
Click Create Incident.
See image.
Group the alerts by category (Alert First Seen, Alert Last Seen, Alert Tags, etc.).
Refresh the alerts table to reflect the most current information.
Export the list of alerts and their associated details as a CSV file.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
View the list of alerts. For each alert, you can see:
ID: The unique identifier of the alert.
Severity: The severity level of the alert (Critical, High, Low, Medium, or None).
Severity Score: The severity score of the alert.
Title: The title of the alert.
Created: The date the alert was created.
Sources: The source of the alert (alerts triggered by Zscaler have the Zscaler logo).
Tactic: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic for which the alert is triggered.
Technique: The MITRE ATT&CK technique for which the alert is triggered.
Click the alert row to view its details.
